questions.stem: Maintenance records show the last transponder inspection was performed on September 1, 2014. The next inspection will be due no later than
With respect to the certification of airmen, which are categories of aircraft?
options: Single-engine land and sea, multiengine land and sea.

questions.stem: A flashing white light signal from the control tower to a taxiing aircraft is an indication to
options: taxi only on taxiways and not cross runways.
return to the starting point on the airport.

questions.stem: During operations outside controlled airspace at altitudes of more than 1,200 feet AGL, but less than 10,000 feet MSL, the minimum flight visibility for day VFR flight is
Unless otherwise authorized, two-way radio communications with Air Traffic Control are required for landings or takeoffs at all towered airports
options: only when weather conditions are less than VFR.
within Class D airspace only when weather conditions are less than VFR.

questions.stem: During operations outside controlled airspace at altitudes of more than 1,200 feet AGL, but less than 10,000 feet MSL, the minimum distance below clouds requirement for VFR flight at night is

Pre-takeoff briefing of passengers about the use of seat belts for a flight is the responsibility of
A 100-hour inspection was due at 3302.5 hours. The 100-hour inspection was actually done at 3309.5 hours. When is the next 100-hour inspection due?
When speaking to a flight service weather briefer, you should state
options: the pilot in command`s full name and address.
whether the flight is VFR or IFR.

questions.stem: Why is frost considered hazardous to flight?
options: Frost changes the basic aerodynamic shape of the airfoils, thereby increasing lift.
Frost slows the airflow over the airfoils, thereby increasing control effectiveness.
Frost spoils the smooth flow of air over the wings, thereby decreasing lifting capability.

questions.stem: What action should a pilot take when operating under VFR in a Military Operations Area (MOA)?
options: Obtain a clearance from the controlling agency prior to entering the MOA.
Operate only on the airways that transverse the MOA.
Exercise extreme caution when military activity is being conducted.

questions.stem: Unless otherwise authorized, if flying a transponder equipped aircraft, a pilot should squawk which VFR code?
What is one purpose of wing flaps?
options: To enable the pilot to make steeper approaches to a landing without increasing the airspeed.
To relieve the pilot of maintaining continuous pressure on the controls.
To decrease wing area to vary the lift.

(Refer to FAA-CT-8080-2H, Figure 35.) Determine the approximate manifold pressure setting with 2,450 RPM to achieve 65 percent maximum continuous power at 6,500 feet with a temperature of 36°F higher than standard.
The term 'angle of attack' is defined as the angle between the
options: chord line of the wing and the relative wind.
airplane's longitudinal axis and that of the air striking the airfoil.
airplane's center line and the relative wind.

questions.stem: When the course deviation indicator (CDI) needle is centered using a VOR test signal (VOT), the omnibearing selector (OBS) and the TO/FROM indicator should read
options: 180° FROM, only if the pilot is due north of the VOT.
0° TO or 180° FROM, regardless of the pilot`s position from the VOT.
0° FROM or 180° TO, regardless of the pilot`s position from the VOT.

questions.stem: (Refer to FAA-CT-8080-2H, Figure 26, area 2.) The day VFR visibility and cloud clearance requirements to operate over the town of Cooperstown, after departing and climbing out of the Cooperstown Airport at or below 700 feet AGL are
options: 1 mile and 1,000 feet above, 500 feet below, and 2,000 feet horizontally from clouds.

questions.stem: (Refer to FAA-CT-8080-2H, Figure 52.) What is the recommended communications procedure for landing at Lincoln Municipal during the hours when the tower is not in operation?
options: Monitor airport traffic and announce your position and intentions on 118.5 MHz.
Contact UNICOM on 122.95 MHz for traffic advisories.
Monitor ATIS for airport conditions, then announce your position on 122.95 MHz.

A pilot and two passengers landed on a 2,100 foot east-west gravel strip with an elevation of 1,800 feet. The temperature is warmer than expected and after computing the density altitude it is determined the takeoff distance over a 50 foot obstacle is 1,980 feet. The airplane is 75 pounds under gross weight. What would be the best choice?
options: Taking off into the headwind will give the extra climb-out time needed.
Try a takeoff without the passengers to make sure the climb is adequate.
Wait until the temperature decreases, and recalculate the takeoff performance.

questions.stem: If an aircraft is equipped with a fixed-pitch propeller and a float-type carburetor, the first indication of carburetor ice would most likely be
options: a drop in oil temperature and cylinder head temperature.

questions.stem: (Refer to FAA-CT-8080-2H, Figure 20, area 1.) The NALF Fentress (NFE) Airport is in what type of airspace?
While on a VFR cross country and not in contact with ATC, what frequency would you use in the event of an emergency?
ATC advises, "traffic 12 o'clock." This advisory is relative to your
Which statement relates to Bernoulli's principle?
options: For every action there is an equal and opposite reaction.
An additional upward force is generated as the lower surface of the airfoil deflects air downward.
Air traveling faster over the curved upper surface of an airfoil causes lower pressure on the top surface.

questions.stem: Deviation error of the magnetic compass is caused by
options: certain metals and electrical systems within the aircraft.
the difference in location of true north and magnetic north.

questions.stem: When executing an emergency approach to land in a single-engine airplane, it is important to maintain a constant glide speed because variations in glide speed will
options: increase the chances of shock cooling the engine.
assure the proper descent angle is maintained until entering the flare.
nullify all attempts at accuracy in judgment of gliding distance and landing spot.

questions.stem: How far will an aircraft travel in 7.5 minutes with a ground speed of 114 knots?

(Refer to FAA-CT-8080-2H, Figure 8.) What is the effect of a temperature increase from 35 to 50°F on the density altitude if the pressure altitude remains at 3,000 feet MSL?
The Aeronautical Information Manual (AIM) specifically encourages pilots to turn on their landing lights when operating below 10,000 feet, day or night, and especially when operating
options: within 15 miles of a towered airport.

questions.stem: When making routine transponder code changes, pilots should avoid inadvertent selection of which code?
A pilot experiencing the effects of hyperventilation should be able to restore the proper carbon dioxide level in the body by
options: slowing the breathing rate, breathing into a paper bag, or talking aloud.
breathing spontaneously and deeply or gaining mental control of the situation.
increasing the breathing rate in order to increase lung ventilation.

questions.stem: This sign confirms your position on
From the cockpit, this marking confirms the aircraft to be
options: on a taxiway, about to enter runway zone.
on a runway, about to clear.
near an instrument approach clearance zone.

questions.stem: (Refer to FAA-CT-8080-2H, Figure 78.) What are the basic VFR weather minima required to takeoff from the Onawa, IA (K36) airport during the day?
options: 3 statute miles visibility, 500 feet below the clouds, 1,000 feet above the clouds, and 2,000 feet horizontally from the clouds.

questions.stem: If Receiver Autonomous Integrity Monitoring (RAIM) capability is lost in-flight,
options: the pilot may still rely on GPS derived altitude for vertical information.
the pilot has no assurance of the accuracy of the GPS position.
GPS position is reliable provided at least 3 GPS satellites are available.

questions.stem: You plan to phone a weather briefing facility for preflight weather information. You should
options: provide the number of occupants on board.
begin with your route of flight.

questions.stem: Your cousin wants you to take him flying. You must have made at least three takeoffs and three landings in your aircraft within the preceding
In what flight condition are torque effects more pronounced in a single-engine airplane?
options: Low airspeed, high power, high angle of attack.
Low airspeed, low power, low angle of attack.
High airspeed, high power, high angle of attack.

questions.stem: The wind at 5,000 feet AGL is southwesterly while the surface wind is southerly. This difference in direction is primarily due to
options: stronger pressure gradient at higher altitudes.
friction between the wind and the surface.
stronger Coriolis force at the surface.

questions.stem: Eye movements during daytime collision avoidance scanning should
options: not exceed 10 degrees and view each sector at least 1 second.
be 30 degrees and view each sector at least 3 seconds.
use peripheral vision by scanning small sectors and utilizing off-center viewing.

questions.stem: When there is a temperature inversion, you would expect to experience
options: clouds with extensive vertical development above an inversion aloft.
good visibility in the lower levels of the atmosphere and poor visibility above an inversion aloft.
an increase in temperature as altitude increases.

Each person who holds a pilot certificate or a medical certificate shall present it for inspection upon the request of any
options: authorized representative of the Department of Transportation.
person in a position of authority.
questions.note: Contested: 14 CFR 61.3(l) also lists any Federal, State or local law enforcement officer. The long-standing FAA key for this item is A.

Unless otherwise authorized, which situation requires Automatic Dependent Surveillance-Broadcast (ADS-B)?
options: Landing at an airport with an operating control tower.
Overflying Class C airspace below 10,000 feet MSL.
Flying under the shelf of Class C airspace.
